messages:
jen-customer: hey team, heads up — our prod deploys started failing after last night's sa token rotation. CI job error is 403 from the /v1/deploy endpoint. not sure if this is a permission or TTL issue

alex: thanks for flagging — can you paste the exact error snippet from the pipeline? and which runner (github actions / gitlab) you saw this on?

jen-customer: here's the failing line from the job log:
```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{
  \"error\": \"insufficient_scope\",
  \"message\": \"service account token missing scope:deploy.write\"
}
```
We use gitlab-runner hosted, and the job uses the CI service account that was rotated at 02:13 UTC. deploys were fine earlier in the night.

maria-support: got it. quick Qs: is the pipeline using an ephemeral OIDC token or a long-lived service-account key? and did you update any runner config?

jen-customer: we switched from long-lived JSON key to ephemeral tokens via our credential-rotation script (vault -> generate short-lived) to satisfy security. rotation job sets `CI_SA_TOKEN` and writes to gitlab secret variables. nothing else changed.

patrick-eng: probable cause: the rotation window for the ephemeral token might be shorter than the token cache TTL used by our deployment proxy. if the proxy caches principal->scope mappings for X minutes, and rotation created a new principal id, you'll see a scope mismatch until cache invalidation. did your rotation change the `sub` or `kid` on the token?

jen-customer: i think rotation preserves the SA id, only the signature and expiry change. vault issue logs show tokens with `exp` ~ 5m after issuance.

sam-devex: couple notes: 1) our `/v1/deploy` endpoint checks both token expiry and a cached grant table keyed by `token_id`. if rotation replaces token_id, the grant table entry isn't found until re-sync. 2) short expiry (5m) can race with queued deploy machines that reused the previous token context.

deploy-bot: notice: canary-deploy-447 failed at 1787654330 with status 403 (insufficient_scope). auto-retry disabled.

alex: to triage, please run a repro with verbose headers. the support repro step: run `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $CI_SA_TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/deploy` right after rotation and again 2m later, capture `x-grant-cache` header and `x-auth-validated-at` times.

jen-customer: doing now — first attempt immediately after rotation:
```
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
x-grant-cache: miss
x-auth-validated-at: 2026-02-15T02:13:41Z
{\"error\":\"insufficient_scope\"}
```
second attempt ~90s later:
```
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
x-grant-cache: populated
x-auth-validated-at: 2026-02-15T02:15:12Z
{\"status\":\"accepted\"}
```
So looks like a ~90s window where the token couldn't be used.

patrick-eng: that matches cache warmup. By design we accept short-lived tokens, but there's a tradeoff: when token_id rotates we rely on background sync from the control-plane to refresh grant entries. normally sync <60s but can spike during high churn.

maria-support: two possible fixes: 1) increase rotation overlap (issue pre-signed transitional token valid for extra TTL) so old and new tokens both valid for a short period; 2) invalidate grant cache faster on rotation via a webhook. which is easier for your infra?

jen-customer: option 1 requires changes to our vault rotation script — easier for us. option 2 would need redwood to accept a cache-flush hook — do you support that?

sam-devex: we don't expose a customer-facing cache invalidation webhook today. we can add a recommended mitigation: create a 120s overlap where the rotation job issues new token but keeps the previous token valid for 2m. That avoids the race. We'll add a doc snippet.

alex: short-term workaround: set your rotation script to mint tokens with `exp` that is now + 5m and set `not-before` to now-30s, then swap variable after verifying deploy success. longer term we should improve our sync heuristics.

jen-customer: thanks — we'll try overlap and report back. one more ask: can you confirm least-privilege scopes required for deploy? our script currently gives `deploy.read,deploy.write,logs.read` but the error said missing `deploy.write`.

patrick-eng: required scopes for the deploy flow: `deploy.write` and `artifacts.read` for standard deploys. `logs.read` optional. if your SA doesn't have `artifacts.read` some jobs that fetch build artifacts will 403 later.

jen-customer: noted — will add `artifacts.read`.

maria-support: follow-up: if you want, we can run a simulated mass-rotation on a staging account to measure the cache-safety window (we can coordinate a time). would that help?

jen-customer: yes please — staging test would be great. can we schedule for tomorrow 03:00 UTC?

sam-devex: scheduled. i'll provision a staging SA and a rotation harness that toggles tokens every 30s for 10 cycles, and collect `x-grant-cache` metrics and deploy success rate. will share results in this thread. :rocket: 

alex: for internal follow-up, i'll open ENG-INVEST ticket to evaluate exposing a cache invalidation webhook or shortening sync latency. tagging @patrick-eng for scope.

patrick-eng: got it — will investigate kernel of sync path (control-plane -> grants cache) and measure tail latency. we can likely trim 30-60s with targeted work.

jen-customer: thanks all, appreciate the quick help. i'll update after staging run. :thumbsup:
